analysis.title: Third Quarter Ends With Surging Yields Closing At 24 Year High... As Stocks Yawn
key_insights: The 10Y Treasury yield hit 5.30% on Oct 1, 2026, the 7th consecutive monthly rise. That passes the 6-month streak of 2023, when stocks fell on stagflation fears.

The real 10Y yield is up 57bp in a month. Goldman (Pasquariello) says this triggered its 2-standard-deviation (~50bp) monthly 'strain' rule historically linked to negative equity returns. Stocks have not sold off this time.

Cooler-than-expected PCE was largely a methodology change. Supercore PCE jumped the most in months after 'Other Services' rose by a record amount. October Fed hike odds fell to 37%, half the level two days earlier.
Williams said on Sep 30 that only one more hike is needed 'late this year.'
Rates rose even as oil fell for much of the day. Goldman Delta-One head Privorotsky calls this divergence the biggest risk for stocks.

Breadth is very weak under a stable index. The median stock is down 5% in the past month, the S&P is unchanged, and semis +6% in the month are what hold the S&P up. The equal-weight S&P 500 had its seventh straight weekly decline, seen only in 2002 and 2022.
The RSP (equal-weight ETF) to S&P ratio hit an all-time low. The S&P had a 12th consecutive day of more 52-week lows than highs (17 of the past 18) while at all-time highs.
The gap between index calm and individual-stock volatility is the widest since 2000, per Goldman.

Credit is widening. CCC OAS is 998bp (+140bp in a month), HY OAS 309bp (+43bp in a week), CDX HY 337.2, and IG all-in yield 6.48%, the highest since 2004. Oracle is the fulcrum, with CDS at a record wide.
The MOVE index hit a post-war high of 110, with the divergence from the S&P the largest on record.
Q3 recap from Rabobank: S&P +2.3% q-o-q vs +14.9% in Q2. US 2s are 4.90% (+72bp), 10s 5.24% (+76bp), 30s 5.57% (+60bp). Global yields also rose sharply.
Central banks hiked in Q3: the RBA, ECB, BOJ and the Fed. The RBA hiked again on Sep 30 and is expected to hike again in the new year.
Brent is about $104 vs $73 at the start of Q3. The 3-2-1 crack spread is $62 vs $17. The FT notes oil and Treasury yields are in their tightest relationship since 1990.

Goldman's high-beta momentum basket fell for the first time after 12 straight up days. Shorts are being covered and software is outperforming semis. JBL fell 7% on a beat/raise, weighing on sentiment into MU's print that night.
Goldman desk: hedge funds are small net sellers with the short ratio below 40%, and long-only funds are +8% better to buy, with demand in software and mega tech.

market_movers.rationale: Fell 7% on a beat/raise, weighing on semis/hardware sentiment ahead of MU's print.
Reports earnings the night of Oct 1. Sentiment into the print is weighed by the JBL reaction and software outperforming semis.
Oracle CDS hit a record wide this week and its bonds are falling. It is described as the fulcrum security in credit stress tied to data center buildout.
Gave back some of the prior day's gains tied to OpenAI developer day.

sector_views.rationale: Semis' 6% gain in the past month is the only thing keeping the S&P afloat, while software is outperforming semis on the day.
Goldman's desk sees long-only demand across software and mega tech, and software is outperforming semis.

FDS rose 4% on a mixed print and outlook (reported).
MU reports the night of Oct 1; sentiment into the print is cautious.

Refined product costs matter more than crude. Rabobank puts the effective oil total at $166 vs $90.

risk_factors: A rates and credit selloff continuing while the S&P holds up at highs on narrow mega-cap leadership.
Rates rising while oil falls, which Privorotsky calls the biggest risk for stocks.
The bubble in AI/semis depends on new debt flows funding heavy cash burn, and credit stress in data center names (CCC bonds, Oracle) threatens that.
A yen carry trade unwind if USD/JPY keeps moving sharply.
Emerging market FX slipping against the dollar, ex-CNY.
October seasonal volatility and the midterm elections.
vol_and_positioning: MOVE index at 110, a post-war high, with the biggest divergence from the S&P on record.
The gap between index volatility and individual-stock volatility is the widest since 2000.
The Goldman desk says the hedge fund short ratio below 40% looks like risk reduction ahead of MU and quarter-end.
Long-only funds are +8% better to buy, with notable demand in software and mega tech.
Goldman's high-beta momentum basket fell for the first time after 12 consecutive days higher.
Shorts are being covered, with software outperforming semis.
geopolitical: Rabobank refers to scarce diesel as a driver of Q3 inflation and rate-hike pressure.
The FT notes oil prices and US Treasury yields are in their tightest relationship since 1990.
US midterm elections follow in the fourth quarter; the author expects a Democratic sweep in Congress.

tension_points.bull_case: Mega-cap tech and semis (+6% in a month) keep the S&P at all-time highs, and Goldman's desk sees long-only buyers (+8% better to buy) in software and mega tech.
tension_points.bear_case: The median stock is down 5% in a month, the equal-weight S&P has fallen seven straight weeks, and the RSP/SPX ratio is at an all-time low. Breadth gaps this large last appeared in 2000.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman's high-beta momentum basket turning down after 12 straight up days, or a megacap tech selloff, would remove the support holding the index up.

tension_points.bull_case: Cooler headline PCE and lower October hike odds (37%) with Williams signaling only one more hike late this year.
tension_points.bear_case: The real 10Y is up 57bp in a month, breaching Goldman's 2-SD speed limit that historically precedes equity selloffs. Credit spreads and MOVE are also stressed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A real 10Y move of more than 50bp in a month has historically meant stocks 'got hammered,' so a selloff in megacap tech would confirm the bear case.
